item.title: DevSparks 2026 heads to Delhi to explore agentic AI and the future of software development
item.description: YourStory’s flagship developer summit makes its Delhi NCR debut on December 5, bringing together developers, technology leaders, startups, and enterprises for hands-on sessions on AI, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, and emerging technologies.
item.content:encoded:
As AI changes how software is developed, tested, and deployed, developers are having to learn new tools and adapt to new ways of working. From autonomous coding agents and multi-agent systems to AI-powered infrastructure and cybersecurity, the technologies shaping software development are evolving rapidly.

Against this backdrop, DevSparks 2026, YourStory’s flagship developer summit, will make its Delhi NCR debut on December 5, bringing together developers, startups, enterprises, and Global Capability Centres (GCCs) for a day of technical deep dives, hands-on sessions, and discussions on the future of software development.

Following editions in Pune, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Chennai, the Delhi event will be held at Crowne Plaza, Gurugram. More than 500 developers are expected to attend, with over 15 technology leaders taking the stage and more than 10 deep-dive sessions planned.

Across its four previous editions, DevSparks has brought together more than 27,000 developers, 173 speakers, and 50 partners.

DevSparks 2026 is a nationwide initiative aimed at equipping India's developer community with skills in coding agents, agentic AI, multi-agent orchestrators, AI SDKs, and GenAI tools that can improve productivity. Delhi NCR's strong developer community, startup ecosystem, and growing enterprise and GCC presence make it the natural next stop for the summit.

Delhi NCR's growing technology ecosystem

Delhi NCR is already one of India's leading startup hubs. According to Tracxn’s Delhi NCR Tech Annual Funding Report 2025, tech companies in the region raised $2.9 billion in 2025, with autotech leading the way with $1.4 billion. 

Delhi-based tech firms accounted for 51% of all funding raised by tech companies across the region in 2025. 

It was also a big year for exits: 19 companies went public, including Lenskart, Physics Wallah, and Pine Labs, while Delhivery bought Ecom Express for $165 million and Everstone Capital acquired Wingify for $200 million.

The Delhi government is taking steps to further strengthen the ecosystem.

The Delhi Start-up and Incubation Policy 2026, approved in July, provides for Rs 400 crore over five years to support incubation infrastructure, mentorship, and incentives for local entrepreneurs.

In October, the Delhi Cabinet also approved the Go-Delhi Foundation, with an initial outlay of Rs 50 crore. The initiative aims to give startups and MSMEs access to product engineering, prototyping and testing facilities.

The government’s draft IT Policy 2026–2031 proposes setting up more than 200 GCCs and training five to six lakh young people by 2031 in areas such as AI, cloud computing, cybersecurity, and data analytics.

It also proposes a Delhi State Data Centre, expected to become operational by 2027, and AI computing credits among other incentives.

These initiatives could create more opportunities for developers working in AI, cloud infrastructure, and cybersecurity, while strengthening the region’s technology ecosystem.

Agentic AI takes centre stage

Agentic AI is becoming an important area of focus for developers and enterprises, and will be a key part of the DevSparks Delhi agenda.

Sessions will explore how to build autonomous agentic systems and develop multi-agent orchestration for coding, workflows, and business operations.

Developers will also examine real-world applications of multimodal AI, including systems that work with text, code, images, video, and speech in production environments.

Building and scaling AI applications

Beyond agentic AI, the summit will examine what it takes to move AI applications from prototypes to production.

Sessions will cover building applications with AI-first frameworks, integrating AI into sectors such as fintech, healthcare, commerce, manufacturing and agritech, and using Edge AI and the Internet of Things (IoT).

The programme will also look at how AI-driven testing can improve developer productivity.

On the infrastructure side, discussions will cover AI-optimised cloud systems, chips, and accelerators, along with multi-cloud, hybrid, and sovereign cloud models for enterprises.

Other areas of focus include data pipelines, governance, cybersecurity threats, and AI-driven defences.

GCCs, skills, and emerging opportunities

With GCCs an important part of Delhi's technology growth plans, DevSparks will also examine how enterprises and GCCs are preparing their workforces for new technologies.

Sessions will look at trends in upskilling, hiring, and workforce readiness as AI becomes increasingly integrated with other technologies.

The discussions will focus on the skills developers need to remain relevant and the opportunities emerging within India’s leading technology enterprises and GCCs.

A day of learning for developers

DevSparks Delhi will offer developers opportunities to learn through technical deep dives, workshops, masterclasses, and real-world case studies.

The sessions are designed to help participants apply AI to practical problems, explore technological advances beyond AI, and identify new career opportunities.

As AI becomes more widely used in software development and enterprise technology, the summit will focus on the tools, skills, and technical knowledge developers need to build and deploy applications.

DevSparks Delhi 2026 will take place on December 5 at Crowne Plaza, Gurugram. Register now to secure your spot. 

Edited by Teja Lele

item.title: Why AI’s biggest challenge lies beneath the model
item.description: At TechSparks 2026, Michael Cronin of Couchbase explained why fragmented data infrastructure remains a major barrier to enterprise AI adoption and why companies need to fix their data systems before scaling AI applications.
item.content:encoded:
AI models are becoming increasingly accessible, but turning them into products that work reliably remains a challenge, particularly when enterprises are dealing with fragmented data infrastructure.

At TechSparks 2026, Michael Cronin, Vice President, Sales, Asia-Pacific, Japan & India, Couchbase, joined Shivani Muthanna, Senior Director – Strategic Content & Video, YourStory, for a discussion on moving AI beyond experimentation, production failures, governance challenges, customer experience, and India's growing role in AI innovation.

AI’s missing link: the data layer

Over the decades, large enterprises have adopted different databases and point solutions to address specific problems. While each solved an immediate need, the result has often been a fragmented data layer, with multiple systems that struggle to work together.

Cronin sees this fragmentation as a major barrier to AI adoption. Citing industry estimates, he said 70–80% of AI development projects never reach production, while an MIT study found that 95% fail to become profitable.

Couchbase’s operational data platform is designed to address this challenge by helping enterprises consolidate their data infrastructure.

Rather than trying to fix everything at once, Cronin advised companies to start small.

“My advice to founders and enterprises that are struggling with the fragmentation of the data layer is to pick your most critical use cases first,” he said.

Cronin cited the example of Tesco, the UK retailer with a large global Capability Center (GCC) in Bengaluru. Its multiple systems were affecting customer experience, particularly during busy shopping periods such as Black Friday and weekends.

Tesco began consolidating its data layer, starting with a single instance and use case before extending the effort across its technology stack.

The consolidation enabled the retailer to handle millions of transactions per second with sub-millisecond latency. According to Cronin, the example shows how companies can begin addressing fragmentation through a single use case before expanding the changes across their operations.

AI moves at machine speed. Can data keep up?

The pressure to develop AI products has led many enterprises to prioritize models and applications. However, pilots often run on small datasets in controlled environments, leaving organizations unprepared for the demands of production.

Cronin pointed to the growing scale of machine-generated traffic.

“Eighteen months ahead of schedule, machine traffic has overtaken human traffic on the internet. That’s the AI scale. That’s the machine speed scale that enterprises need to operate on,” he said.

When AI applications encounter real-world workloads, fragmented data systems can prevent them from operating reliably at scale.

The growing use of AI agents adds to the challenge. As agents become more autonomous and take on decision-making responsibilities, enterprises need to ensure they can access the right data while working within appropriate governance frameworks.

Fragmented systems can make communication and governance more difficult, limiting the ability of agents to operate autonomously.

Cronin also urged enterprises to reconsider how they allocate their AI investments. While models are evolving rapidly, enterprise data remains a critical asset.

“The models are rentable. Today’s best model is yesterday's newspaper. The true asset for the enterprise is the data,” he said.

More API layers aren't the answer

As enterprises began recognizing that fragmented data was holding back their AI initiatives, many responded by adding APIs and connectors to link existing systems.

Cronin cautioned that this approach could introduce further complexity rather than solve the underlying problem. Each additional connection brings latency, risk, and another potential point of failure.

Instead, he recommended consolidating the data layer so applications and AI agents can communicate with it more directly, bringing data closer to customers.

According to Cronin, many enterprises, including large GCCs in India, are now reassessing their architecture to address data fragmentation. Without these changes, further investment in AI development could lead to the same problems.

Consolidating data can also improve customer experience by helping systems manage growing demand, remain available and respond quickly.

As customers expect more from AI-powered services, having data available at the edge is becoming increasingly important.

India: From back office to innovation leader

Cronin observed that business cultures vary across the Asia-Pacific region, but fragmented data infrastructure remains a common challenge for AI adoption.

At the same time, India is becoming an important centre for AI innovation and decision-making.

He noted that 80% of Couchbase's top 50 global accounts have a significant presence in India, with much of their AI innovation and leadership based in the country.

Couchbase is also expanding its presence in India, with its Asia-Pacific headquarters moving to Bengaluru. Its Indian enterprise customers include Air India, Airtel, BigBasket, and Mahindra Finance.

According to Cronin, India’s role in global business has moved beyond cost savings, with innovation, leadership, and important business decisions increasingly taking place here.

He cited Air India's next-generation entertainment platform, which is being built on Couchbase. The platform aims to provide passengers with personalized shopping and entertainment experiences even when an aircraft is offline.

For Cronin, the project shows how Indian enterprises are using technology to improve customer experiences under real-world operating conditions.

item.title: 5 lessons from 30 Something Millionaire by Mohit Chawla
item.description: Discover five valuable lessons from Mohit Chawla's 30 Something Millionaire on building wealth, financial independence, discipline and long-term success.
item.content:encoded:
Becoming wealthy is a goal many people aspire to achieve, but building lasting wealth requires more than earning a high salary or finding the right investment opportunity. It involves developing the right habits, making informed financial decisions and understanding the importance of patience.

In 30 Something Millionaire: How NOT to Ace the Rat Race… author Mohit Chawla shares his journey to financial independence and the principles that helped him become a self-made dollar millionaire in his early thirties.

Drawing from his experience across investment banking, private equity, hedge funds, entrepreneurship and real estate, Chawla explores how consistency, discipline and the power of compounding can shape financial and professional success.

5 Key lessons from 30 Something Millionaire

1. Consistency matters more than quick success

Many people look for shortcuts to achieve financial success. They want quick returns, rapid career growth and immediate results. However, building wealth is rarely an overnight process.

One of the central ideas in 30 Something Millionaire is the importance of consistency. Whether it involves saving money, investing regularly, developing professional skills or building a business, small efforts made repeatedly can create meaningful results over time.

Chawla's journey highlights how consistent decisions and disciplined actions can contribute to long-term financial independence.

The lesson is simple: Instead of constantly searching for shortcuts, focus on building habits that support your goals. Consistency may seem slow initially, but its impact becomes more visible with time.

2. Understand the power of compounding

Compounding is one of the most important concepts discussed in the book. Most people learn about compound interest during their school years, but not everyone understands how powerful it can be when applied to everyday financial decisions.

Compounding allows money to generate returns, which can then generate additional returns over time. The longer an investment remains invested, the greater the potential impact of this process.

However, the idea of compounding is not limited to money. Knowledge, experience and professional skills can also grow through continuous learning and practical application.

For instance, reading regularly, learning new skills and gaining experience in your field can gradually create opportunities that were not available earlier.

The lesson is to start early, remain consistent and give your investments, knowledge and efforts enough time to grow.

3. Financial independence requires discipline

Financial independence is not simply about earning more money. It also involves understanding how to manage what you earn.

A higher income does not automatically lead to wealth if spending increases at the same pace. Developing financial discipline means making thoughtful decisions about expenses, savings and investments.

In 30 Something Millionaire, Chawla discusses the importance of personal financial habits, including saving and investing, as part of the journey towards building wealth.

Rather than spending everything you earn, it is important to create a financial plan that prioritises your long-term goals.

The lesson is that wealth is built not only through income but also through how effectively you manage and invest your money.

4. Build your career with a long-term perspective

Professional success is another important aspect of the book. Career growth is often viewed through immediate achievements, such as promotions, salary increases or prestigious job titles.

However, building a successful career requires developing a broader understanding of your industry, improving decision-making abilities and learning how businesses operate.

Chawla's professional experience across investment banking, private equity, hedge funds, real estate and entrepreneurship offers insights into the importance of understanding different business environments.

The book encourages readers to look beyond short-term career milestones and focus on building skills, gaining experience and identifying opportunities that can create long-term value.

The lesson is to treat your career as a long-term investment. Every new skill, professional relationship and experience can contribute to your future growth.

5. Learn from successful people and their experiences

You do not always have to learn everything through personal mistakes. Sometimes, understanding the experiences of people who have already achieved success can help you make better decisions.

One of the three broad categories of learnings in 30 Something Millionaire focuses on timeless wisdom drawn from successful individuals across different fields.

Their experiences can offer valuable perspectives on leadership, decision-making, business strategies, financial management and personal development.

However, learning from others does not mean copying their journeys. Every individual has different circumstances, opportunities and challenges. The important thing is to understand the principles behind their decisions and apply the relevant lessons to your own life.

The lesson is to remain curious, keep learning and seek knowledge beyond your immediate professional or personal environment.

Final thoughts

30 Something Millionaire: How NOT to Ace the Rat Race… Yet Be Successful and Wealthy by Mohit Chawla offers a practical perspective on building wealth, developing professional skills and making better life decisions.

One of its biggest takeaways is that success is not necessarily about earning the most money or following a conventional career path. It is about making consistent decisions, understanding the power of compounding, practising financial discipline and investing in personal growth.

Whether you are an aspiring entrepreneur, a young professional or someone working towards financial independence, the book offers lessons that can help you approach money, work and life with a longer-term perspective.

item.title: How Pine Labs is building for the agent economy: CTO Sanjeev Kumar on trust, control and execution
item.description: At TechSparks 2026, Pine Labs Chief Technology Officer, Sanjeev Kumar showcased how developers, merchants, and teams can put AI agents to work, backed by controls that keep them accountable.
item.content:encoded:
AI agents are starting to run real parts of a business, from finding customers to processing complaints. For banks, fintech companies, and enterprises, that raises a basic question: how far can an agent be trusted to act on its own?

Pine Labs is addressing this question by building an ecosystem that enables AI agents to take on tasks across commerce while keeping their actions accountable. Speaking at its product showcase at TechSparks 2026, Sanjeev Kumar, CTO, Pine Labs, said, “We have tried to make AI a first-class citizen in our ecosystem.”

Over the past 18 months, Pine Labs has been building a commerce operating system around AI agents, combining tools to manage their permissions and track their actions with applications for merchants and enterprise teams. Its Agent Store will open the ecosystem to third-party developers building for merchants and banks.

Building trust into AI agents

For agents to operate in banking and enterprise environments, organizations need to know what they are authorized to do and how their actions can be audited. Pine Labs has developed Grantex, which Kumar described as ‘Open Authorization 2.0 for AI agents’. It assigns each agent a defined set of permissions, an expiry, and a record of the human who authorized it. If an agent authorized to read and draft emails attempts to send one, the action can be blocked and its permissions revoked, including those of any child agents. A tamper-proof, hash-chain audit trail records its actions.

Kumar outlined the work involved in connecting tools and systems, setting up retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), running continuous evaluations, and deciding where human intervention is necessary. These components need to work together before an agent can reliably handle tasks in an enterprise environment.

Pine Labs first deployed the technology across its compliance, finance, HR, and marketing teams, with processing taking place within its own environment. The company is also implementing it with banks in India and overseas.

From cyber fraud complaints to faster resolution

Cora, Pine Labs’ compliance and resolution agent, takes cyber fraud complaints from intake to closure. It matches complaints to transactions, categorizes them, routes them to relevant teams, and prepares responses for review. Kumar said Pine Labs has been able to close some complaints on the same day, compared with the typical three-to-five-day turnaround.

The agent records a 15-step trace of its work, including validation, transaction lookups, settlement checks, and team notifications, along with supporting evidence and confidence levels. When a system connector is unavailable, Cora can use robotic process automation (RPA). In the demonstration, it accessed the government cyber police portal and filled in an action-taken form with transaction details and the disputed amount. A human operator retains control of the password and one-time code and reviews the form before submission.

Opening the platform to developers

Having deployed agents across its own compliance, finance, HR and marketing teams, Pine Labs has since opened its platform to developers and merchant partners. The company is also working with banks in India and overseas.

To show how the technology could be applied beyond its own operations, Kumar pointed to a hackathon organized by Pine Labs and The Ken , which drew more than 380 agent submissions from students, fresh graduates, and engineers across India. The winning entry helped people decide what to cook for dinner.

Developers can create skill files, connect tools, and define tasks in plain English, while AgenticOrg provides visibility into agents, confidence scores, and audit trails via Grantex. The AgenticOrg is intended to help third-party developers build applications for merchants and banks using Pine Labs’ infrastructure.

Helping small merchants run ad campaigns

For smaller businesses, Pine Labs has also developed an ads agent accessible through its merchant interface. Merchants connect their Google Ads account, enter details about their business, and provide a brief, budget, and campaign goal. The agent researches local demand and nearby competitors, then generates ad copy for search, display, and YouTube.

Merchants can request changes and approve the campaign before it goes live. The demonstration showed setup taking about two minutes, with campaign performance and lead routing available through the same interface.

Building an ecosystem for commerce

From internal enterprise workflows and cyber fraud resolution to advertising for small businesses, Pine Labs is applying its agent infrastructure to different parts of commerce. Grantex sets guardrails for what agents can do; AgenticOrg helps teams, individuals, and AI enthusiasts build agents, manage work, and execute tasks, and AgenticOrg is intended to let developers build further applications for merchants and banks.

Pine Labs is betting that the future of commerce will be shaped not just by what AI agents can do, but by how reliably they can do it. By combining the infrastructure to govern agents with applications that solve real business problems, the company is looking to make autonomous AI a working part of commerce, for enterprises, banks, and merchants alike.

item.title: VC funding into Indian B2C ecommerce companies dips 33%: Tracxn
item.description: Late- and seed-stage funding nearly halved in the period between January 1 and November 3 this year, while early-stage funding remained stable compared to last year.
item.content:encoded:
Venture capital funding into business-to-consumer (B2C) ecommerce companies in India dropped 33% in the ten months of the year, according to a report by Tracxn.

The report titled 'India B2C E-Commerce' noted that, between January 1, 2026 and November 3, 2026, B2C ecommerce companies raised $1.6 billion across 356 rounds, compared with $2.4 billion from 621 rounds in the similar period of 2025.

According to the report, funding and rounds declined, with late- and seed-stage funding nearly halving, while early-stage funding remained stable in 2026 compared to 2025.

The key funding rounds during the period included FS Life ($110 million), Ultrahuman ($65 million), Yulu ($63 million), Snabbit ($56 million), FirstClub ($55 million), and Nua ($50 million).

Early-stage funding reached $872 million in 2026, up 3% from $846 million in 2025. In contrast, late-stage funding declined 51% to $587 million from $1.2 billion, while seed-stage funding fell 50% to $169 million from $339 million. Early-stage accounted for 54% of total funding in 2026, with 97 rounds, compared with 125 in 2025.

Bengaluru raised $686 million in 2026, accounting for 43% of the $1.6 billion raised for the year till now. Mumbai ranked second, with $286 million, while the third place was taken by Gurugram at $199 million.

On the exit front, acquisitions declined to 19 in 2026 compared with 25 in 2025, while IPOs nearly halved to 7 compared to 13 in 2025. L’Oréal’s acquisition of Innovist for $434 million was the largest acquisition of the year by deal value, while Purple Style Labs recorded the highest market capitalisation among companies that went public in 2026, at $488 million. Astrotalk was the only new unicorn in 2026 from the ecommerce category.

item.title: Razorpay gets Sebi nod for Rs 5,000-6,000 Cr IPO; eyes $5B valuation
item.description: The development comes after Razorpay submitted its draft IPO papers with Sebi through the confidential route in June, initiating the process to tap the public markets.
item.content:encoded:
Fintech firm Razorpay has secured approval from markets regulator Sebi for its proposed initial public offering (IPO) of Rs 5,000-6,000 crore, sources familiar with the development said on Wednesday.

The company is targeting a valuation of around $5 billion through the public offering, they added.

The development comes after Razorpay submitted its draft IPO papers with Sebi through the confidential route in June, initiating the process to tap the public markets.

Founded in 2014 by Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar, Razorpay offers payment acceptance, banking, payouts, payroll, lending and other financial services through an integrated platform.

The company serves millions of businesses across India, ranging from startups and small and medium enterprises to large corporates.

Razorpay attained unicorn status in 2020 and has since expanded beyond payments into a broader financial services ecosystem for businesses. Its offerings enable merchants to manage collections, payouts, payroll, cash flows and access to capital through a single platform.

The company is backed by investors including Peak XV Partners, GIC, Tiger Global, Ribbit Capital, Lone Pine Capital, Alkeon Capital and TCV.

The confidential filing route allows companies to submit draft offer documents to Sebi for review without immediately disclosing sensitive business information to the public.

Rival fintech firm PhonePe's IPO remains temporarily on hold after the company officially paused the process in March 2026 due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia and volatile market conditions. The company intended to raise over $1 billion at a valuation of $9-10.5 billion.

item.title: Frammer AI partners with Collective Newsroom to power BBC News video in India
item.description: Frammer AI will power video workflows, including repurposing, for Collective Newsroom, which produces BBC content in India.
item.content:encoded:
Frammer AI, an AI-native video studio, has partnered with Collective Newsroom, which produces content for the BBC in India in nine languages. Frammer will power Collective Newsroom’s video workflows, including repurposing of content.

According to Frammer, the partnership is helping public service journalism reach more people through digital-first formats.

What the platform does

Frammer automates the main steps of video production and distribution. Its platform takes in content, repurposes and clips it, and publishes it to different digital platforms in one click.

“With Frammer and the ethical use of AI, Collective Newsroom aims to strengthen its ability to deliver creative, credible, and courageous journalism efficiently, without compromising on human judgment, editorial integrity, or public trust,” said Sara Hassan, COO, Collective Newsroom.

Suparna Singh, CEO, Frammer AI, spoke about how the newsroom is approaching the technology. “It’s terrific to see such an experienced team embracing AI responsibly, with editorial rigour and strong brand safety checks at every step,” she said.

The newsroom behind BBC News in India

Four former BBC employees in India founded Collective Newsroom in 2024. It now has more than 250 journalists. It is the sole provider of content for BBC News in India, which covers the television channel, nine Indian-language websites, social media platforms and the BBC News India YouTube channel.

Frammer’s publisher network

The former management team of NDTV set up Frammer AI in 2023. The company says its platform helps publishers move content as quickly as social media demands.

Frammer says it works with some of the world’s largest publishers. These include ABS-CBN in the Philippines, Media Prima in Malaysia and Medialivre in Portugal. In India, it has partnered with The India Today Group, Network 18 and several others.

item.title: Sarva Suvidhaen: Bihar Startup Is Using AI and IoT to Make Indian Railways Smarter
item.description: Bihar-based startup Sarva Suvidhaen is using AI and IoT to modernise Indian Railways, improve operational efficiency, and build smarter railway systems
item.content:encoded:
India’s railway network is one of the largest and most complex public infrastructure systems in the world. Every day, thousands of trains, millions of passengers, freight transportation, stations, tracks, and field teams operate simultaneously. In such a system, even a small delay can have an impact across multiple levels.

Sometimes, reports from the field do not arrive on time. In some cases, data remains scattered across different systems. At times, officials are unable to obtain real-time information about a situation. In such circumstances, technology is no longer just a means of speeding up work; it becomes an important part of better governance and decision-making.

The Bihar-based startup Sarva Suvidhaen is working in this space. The company is developing solutions for railways and other large infrastructure systems with the help of artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), computer vision, and software.

The company was founded by Atul Anand and Srishti. Both have different professional backgrounds, but during the lockdown, they observed a common problem closely. While working from home in Patna, they recognised the need for better data, automation, and real-time monitoring in certain processes of Indian Railways.

This led to the idea of a startup that could use technology to solve ground-level problems in public infrastructure rather than limiting its applications to private companies.

YourStory recently spoke with Atul Anand, CTO (Chief Technology Officer) of Sarva Suvidhaen. He spoke in detail about the company's beginnings, the experience of entrepreneurship in Bihar, the AI and IoT solutions developed for railways, the challenges involved, and future plans.

Atul Anand's story began at a Hindi-medium government school in Bihar. He completed his matriculation through the Bihar Board in 2005. He then pursued his intermediate education at Patna Science College between 2005 and 2007.

He went on to earn a BTech in Computer Science and Engineering from NIT Trichy. After that, he worked in software development roles at companies such as Oracle, BEL, CLS, KPI Partners, IQuanti, and SpotOn.

Srishti began her schooling at the School of Creative Learning. She completed her Class 12 education through the BSEB. She then pursued a BBM from Magadh University and an MBA from Uttarakhand Technical University. She worked at SPVR and Co, Randstad, and Cognizant.

Both had different experiences. Atul had experience in technology and software development, while Srishti had experience in business, management, and operations. This difference later became the company's strength.

Atul explains, “After working in the software development sector for more than 12 years, I felt that the use of technology should not be limited to the needs of companies alone. Our country's large public systems also need it. Srishti encouraged me to think in this direction. We decided to use our technical understanding to work on problems that affect public services and ordinary people.”

The Idea Emerged During the Lockdown

During the lockdown, both were working from home in Patna. During this period, they began looking closely at the everyday processes of Indian Railways. They felt that data, field reporting, and monitoring across such a large network could be made more organised. This was particularly relevant to processes that require information to be collected from different locations and decisions to be made based on it.

Srishti encouraged Atul to use his technical background in this direction. Together, they began exploring ways to connect machine learning (ML), IoT, and software with public infrastructure challenges.

Sarva Suvidhaen focuses on organisations where operations are spread across multiple locations. In such systems, manual reporting and limited data visibility can slow down the decision-making process.

The company operates on a B2B and B2G model. This includes developing software and IoT solutions, along with their deployment, consultancy, and maintenance.

Atul says, “We did not start with a large market study. While living in Patna during the lockdown, we observed some real-world problems. We felt that technologies such as machine learning and IoT could help us understand and solve these problems. I took responsibility for technology, while Srishti worked on the business and operations side. In this way, our respective roles gradually became clear, and Sarva Suvidhaen's work progressed.”

From Homemade Badi to GomatiRoots: Shital Kumari Secures Funding

Making Indian Railways Smarter

The startup has developed several solutions to digitise field operations for Indian Railways. One of these is WagonEye, an AI- and computer vision-based platform. It is used to identify potential defects in the body and undergear of freight and passenger train wagons. In a large network such as the railways, identifying potential problems on time can be important for both safety and operations.

In addition, RailOps is a digital operations platform. It enables railway teams to record and monitor field activities.

SwachhDNR is a web and mobile platform. It has been deployed in the Danapur division, which includes Patna Junction, as well as the Sealdah and Jhansi divisions. It is used to track and assess employee performance.

Through these solutions, the company's effort is to make field data available in digital form and connect it with the decision-making process.

Atul explains, “Our focus is not limited to developing software. We want technology to work where the actual problem exists. Conditions in railway field operations are not always the same. Therefore, it is important for AI models and IoT systems to function reliably in real-world environments. Solutions such as WagonEye, RailOps, and SwachhDNR have been developed with this approach in mind. Our goal is to convert data into information that can support better decision-making at both the field and management levels.”

Funding from Startup Bihar and Google Cloud

Sarva Suvidhaen started through bootstrapping. This means the founders did not take funding from any external investors initially. Both used their personal savings and the earnings from their initial projects.

Later, they received Rs 10 lakh in funding from Startup Bihar. They also received incubation support from IIT Patna and STPI. In addition, the company received Rs 1 crore in credits from Google Cloud. These resources were used to build and scale its AI and IoT infrastructure.

According to the company, it has received a total of Rs 32 lakh in government assistance. In addition, it has raised Rs 60 lakh in external equity funding from two investors.

The experience of working with government institutions gave Sarva Suvidhaen an opportunity to understand several important aspects of business. Large government organisations follow established rules and procedures for procurement. Therefore, building trust and establishing a strong track record are essential when introducing new technology. At the same time, pilot projects and real-world field environments are highly useful for improving deep-tech solutions. These experiences helped the company make its solutions more practical and reliable.

Now Focusing on India's Large Infrastructure Systems

Sarva Suvidhaen has also witnessed growth in its business. In the financial year 2024–25, the company's turnover was approximately Rs 48 lakh. It recorded a profit of around Rs 9 lakh. In the financial year 2025–26, its turnover increased to approximately Rs 1.16 crore. The company's profit stood at around Rs 20 lakh.

The company's revenue model is based on one-time development and integration fees, along with monthly or annual subscriptions and maintenance contracts.

The company now wants to expand its presence across all zones of Indian Railways. Alongside this, it plans to take its solutions into sectors such as logistics, healthcare, and smart cities.

At the technology level, the company is preparing to invest more in edge AI, computer vision, and predictive maintenance.

The incubation centre at IIT Patna has also played an important role in this journey. According to the company, funding, technical support, mentorship, and industry connections helped transform its prototypes into solutions that could be used in the field.

Atul says, “We do not see Sarva Suvidhaen merely as a company working for the railways. Our goal is to become a partner in AI, IoT, and automation for critical infrastructure. To achieve this, we need to make our technology capable of working under different conditions. Going forward, we want to explore opportunities in sectors such as logistics, healthcare, and smart cities, alongside railways. Our belief is that the journey can begin in Bihar, but the solutions should reach across India and, eventually, the world.”

Starting in Bihar, Building Solutions for India, and Expanding Across the World

Sarva Suvidhaen's story is still in its early stages. The company will continue to face challenges such as government procurement processes, long sales cycles, and the large-scale deployment of deep-tech solutions.

However, there is another side to this story. It shows how new opportunities for entrepreneurship and technological talent are taking shape in Bihar. A startup that begins in a city like Patna can develop solutions for one of the largest public infrastructure systems in the country.

The startup ecosystem, incubation centres, government assistance, and support from technical institutions can help such ventures progress beyond their initial stages. Sarva Suvidhaen's journey is an example of this changing environment.

For Atul and Srishti, the direction ahead is clear. They want to work on problems whose impact can be seen on the ground and whose solutions can be deployed at scale.

Their message also reflects this approach: “Start your journey in Bihar, find solutions to India's real problems, and build solutions that the world can adopt as well.”

Sarva Suvidhaen began its journey in Bihar, but its ambitions are not limited to the state. The company is now working on developing solutions that can be used in other large infrastructure sectors, in addition to railways. Through its efforts to solve ground-level problems using AI, IoT, and automation, the company also presents an interesting picture of Bihar's evolving startup ecosystem.

item.title: Cabinet approves Rs 2,814 Cr scheme to promote processing of lithium, nickel
item.description: The scheme aims to develop domestic processing capabilities in India to support value addition within the country, reduce import dependence, and develop value chain.
item.content:encoded:
The government on Wednesday approved a capex support scheme to promote processing of critical minerals lithium and nickel with a financial outlay of Rs 2,814 crore over a period of five years till 2030-31.

The decision was taken at a Union Cabinet meeting under the chairmanship of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

The scheme aims to develop domestic processing capabilities in India to support value addition within the country, reduce import dependence, and develop a value chain.

Under the scheme, capital subsidy of 30% of eligible investment will be provided for setting up four critical mineral processing plants, comprising two lithium processing plants and two nickel processing plants. The maximum capital support will be capped at Rs 500 crore per lithium beneficiary and Rs 900 crore per nickel beneficiary, respectively.

Critical minerals are vital for economic development, national security, and modern clean-energy technologies. They are key components of modern technologies and essential for a low-carbon future. From solar panels and electric vehicles to electronic devices carried in pockets, critical minerals form the foundation of a modern, net-zero economy.

"Our National Critical Mineral Mission has been progressing in a very systematic manner...A scheme for the processing of critical minerals was approved by the Cabinet today," Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw told media.

The processing of critical minerals remains geographically concentrated in a few global locations, leaving global supply chains vulnerable to geopolitical tensions, price volatility, and export or supply restrictions, an official statement said.

This concentration threatens supply chain resilience and economic security, with serious consequences for national security, economic sovereignty, and the timely delivery of decarbonisation goals

At present, India remains substantially dependent on imports for refined intermediates and high-purity materials, owing to the nascent stage of domestic beneficiation and processing infrastructure for critical minerals, including lithium, nickel and cobalt.

Domestic processing capacity for critical minerals remains limited, with commercial-scale projects facing challenges relating to high capital requirements, limited availability of suitable technologies and constrained access to raw materials.

Domestic processing capacity is therefore imperative for maximising value addition, achieving import substitution, and establishing resilient end-to-end value chains.

Against this backdrop, the scheme has been formulated to provide targeted capital expenditure support for setting up of and operationalisation of domestic processing facilities.

The scheme aims to develop processing capabilities to support value addition within the country, reduce import dependence, and develop value chain.

The scheme targets processing of lithium and nickel ores/intermediary products into high purity compounds.

Cobalt is also expected to be recovered as a by-product of nickel production. This will support critical sectors such as electric mobility, Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), electronics, defence and speciality steel.

The proposed scheme, with an overall outlay of Rs 2,814 crore, will be implemented from 2026-27 to 2030-31.

item.title: PhysicsWallah posts Rs 1,242 Cr top-line in Q2; net profit doubles
item.description: PhysicsWallah clocked an operational revenue of Rs 1,242.26 crore in Q2 FY27, up 18.2% YoY, while profit after tax doubled to Rs 142.29 crore, driven by digital scale and operating efficiencies.
item.content:encoded:
The second quarter of the 2027 financial year marked a pivotal turn for PhysicsWallah (PW), as expanding scale and cost efficiencies together yielded a record quarterly top-line and a two-fold growth in net profit.

The edtech firm achieved its highest-ever quarterly revenue, driven by expanding student enrolments and enhanced course realisations. 

Consolidated revenue from operations reached Rs 1,242.26 crore, up 18.2% YoY. Total income, which includes other non-operating receipts, grew 21.5% YoY to Rs 1,334.64 crore. Consolidated profit after tax doubled to Rs 142.29 crore in the second quarter, rising 104.1% YoY from Rs 69.72 crore. 

The net profit in Q2FY27 comes after a loss of Rs 87.04 crore in Q1FY27.

“We delivered record revenue and a sharp improvement in profitability, while our learner base kept widening across K-12, vernacular and new categories. Our focus remains on scaling affordable, tech-led education with disciplined capital allocation,” said Founder and Chief Executive Officer Alakh Pandey.

PW's business operates across two principal delivery channels alongside auxiliary services. The online channel remained the primary engine of top-line growth, generating Rs 693.52 crore in operational revenue during the quarter. This marked a 26.4% YoY surge from Rs 548.72 crore in the year-ago period, representing 55.8% of total revenue from operations. The offline channel contributed Rs 540.87 crore, a 9% YoY rise from Rs 496.10 crore, accounting for 43.5% of operational revenue. 

Other operational streams, encompassing YouTube advertising, hardware device sales, and institutional support services, generated Rs 7.87 crore, growing 22.4% YoY.

Profitability demonstrated substantial expansion as fixed platform, content, and teaching infrastructure costs were distributed across a wider user base.

Profit after tax margin, defined as net earnings divided by operational revenue, widened by 482 basis points to 11.5% from 6.6%. Profit before tax surged 111.6% YoY to Rs 209.15 crore. This figure included a one-off Rs 20 crore exceptional goodwill impairment charge and a Rs 10 crore fair-value gain on financial instruments.

Reported EBITDA under Indian Accounting Standards (IndAS) reached Rs 348 crore, yielding a 28.0% margin compared to Rs 228 crore and a 21.7% margin in the same period last year. Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back fair-value adjustments and lease liabilities, rose to Rs 399 crore at a 32.1% margin against Rs 270 crore and 25.7% previously. Pre-IndAS cash EBITDA grew 45.0% YoY to Rs 233 crore, lifting margins to 18.8% from 15.3%.

Total consolidated expenses for continuing operations stood at Rs 1,105.43 crore. Employee benefits expense formed the largest single cost centre at Rs 522.38 crore, including Rs 482 crore in core salaries and Rs 40 crore in non-cash share-based compensation. Other operational expenses totaled Rs 237.58 crore, with marketing, advertisement, and publicity accounting for Rs 87.92 crore. 

Strategic growth and technology

The online division benefitted from increased student engagement and higher collection realisations. Unique transacting online users grew 12.9% YoY to 1.5 million during the quarter, while average collection per user rose 10.6% YoY to Rs 4,280. 

Growth was bolstered by strong demand for premium course bundles, with collections from Infinity and Infinity Pro collections expanding 49% in the second quarter. 

Higher-value non-medical categories led the expansion, including civil services with a 34.2% increase in average collections, GATE rising 30.7%, foundation courses up 22.6%, and MBA programmes up 21.4%.

The quarter also experienced an operational shift in medical entrance prep demand. Postponement of the NEET UG 2026 exam results to July 16 delayed student enrollments, shifting a major portion of admission activity into the second quarter. Consequently, online NEET enrollments surged over 30% YoY during the three-month period.

In the offline segment, revenue reached Rs 541 crore across 370 physical centres, compared to 314 centres a year earlier. The offline channel recorded a Pre-IndAS EBITDA loss of Rs 8 crore in the second quarter, narrowing from earlier periods as mature centres improved utilisation. 

The company management has intentionally slowed physical expansion to 25-30 new centres annually to focus on centre-level profitability and smaller footprint models.

To streamline capital deployment, PW exited direct student lending by selling the Rs 96 crore loan book of its subsidiary FinZ Finance Private Limited to Auxilo Finserve Private Limited on October 3.

Artificial intelligence integration has expanded operational efficiency across learning platforms. Automated systems resolve 80% of student support queries without human intervention and generate 92% of internal software code, the company said.

The company is developing AI Tuto, a conversational voice-based 1:1 tutor designed to guide students at an estimated cost to serve of Rs 17 per hour.

item.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (November 05, 2026)
item.description: YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, November 05, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
From how KumaonKhand, a social enterprise building a hemp-based ecosystem in Uttarakhand, began as a college project and became a full-time venture in 202, to how PhysicsWallah and Lenskart's doubled their profit in the second quarter of FY27, here are the latest developments across sectors.

Featured Stories

How KumaonKhand is building a hemp ecosystem in Uttarakhand

KumaonKhand, a social enterprise building a hemp-based ecosystem in Uttarakhand, began as a college project and became a full-time venture in 2021 with his mother, Sangeeta and Anuj Sharma, the founder and CEO of Alsisar Impact, a social impact incubator and investment firm.

A problem-mapping exercise through an environmental and social lens pointed toward hemp as a solution.

The Bengaluru-based company said it will use the funds to expand its manufacturing capacity, strengthen research and development, support customer qualification programmes, and grow its engineering and commercial teams. The investment will help altM transition from pilot-scale production to commercial manufacturing.

Read more

Funding News

Venomics AI raises $2.7M pre-seed round led by Speciale Invest, South Park Commons

Bengaluru-based Venomics AI, a biotechnology startup spun out of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), has raised $2.7 million in a pre-seed funding round co-led by Speciale Invest and South Park Commons, with participation from Operators Studio. Co-founded by Kartik Sunagar and Vinay Prabhu, the company uses artificial intelligence, venom biology and laboratory screening to identify venom-derived molecules with therapeutic potential.

The funding will be used to expand its Venom Atlas molecular dataset, strengthen AI and experimental screening capabilities, hire across research and computational science, and validate promising molecules. The startup aims to build a drug discovery platform for global markets.

Other News

Zoho launches restaurant POS platform in India

Zoho has launched a point-of-sale (POS) platform for restaurants in India, with Kolkata-based sweet shop Asha Sweets becoming its first customer. The product is being offered free of charge to restaurants with annual billing of up to Rs 12 lakh, as part of Zoho’s push to bring smaller food businesses onto digital platforms.

In a post on X, Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu said Asha Sweets began using Zoho POS for Restaurants during the festive rush. Zoho’s team visited the outlet to observe how the platform was being used during one of its busiest periods.

Read more

Prodigi Connect partners with Indonesia's Lokanima to develop AI-powered animation for Fun Cican

Dubai-headquartered AI video production company Prodigi Connect has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Lokanima, a creative venture of Indonesia's Singhasari Special Economic Zone, to develop animated content based on Indonesian children's entertainment property Fun Cican. 

The partnership will combine Prodigi Connect's AI-native production capabilities and India-based operations with Lokanima's intellectual property access, local creative direction and Indonesian production talent. Prodigi Connect has already produced an approximately one-minute animation sequence as an initial demonstration. The collaboration aims to reduce the cost and time associated with conventional animation production while expanding the company's presence in international character-based intellectual property development.

75% of Gen Z and Millennials more likely to travel across generations, finds Airbnb survey

Airbnb's 2026 intergenerational travel survey found that 75% of Gen Z and Millennial respondents are more likely to travel with family members across generations. The findings highlight a growing preference for holidays centred on shared experiences, with 55% citing creating memories and 51% strengthening family bonds as key motivations. 

Airbnb reported a more than 55% year-on-year increase in domestic searches for stays by groups of five or more travelling with children or infants. The survey also found that 63% of respondents prioritise relaxing together at their accommodation over sightseeing. Bangalore, Goa, Hyderabad, The Nilgiris and Pondicherry feature among popular domestic destinations.

item.title: Blinkit Ambulance to charge Rs 2,500 for non-emergency cases
item.description: Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal noted that a growing share of bookings for its free ambulance service were for routine checkups, hospital visits and hospital-to-home transfers.
item.content:encoded:
Blinkit Ambulance, the free service from the quick commerce company, will now start charging Rs 2,500 for non-emergency transfers.

“Emergency transfers–free, as always. Non-emergency transfers–₹2,500, charged after the trip. Broadly in line with what private ambulances charge. This money goes to the Eternal Foundation, which runs these ambulances and will help us scale them even further,” Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal said in a post on X.

Goyal noted that Blinkit Ambulance was started as a spirit of service, and in the last two years, it has served around 20,000 emergency cases and more than 42,000 cases in total. “We haven't charged a single rupee for any of them. And we want to keep it that way,” he remarked.

The reason for the change is that a growing share of bookings were for routine checkups, hospital visits and hospital-to-home transfers, the post noted. As Goyal remarked that every such booking requires a fully equipped emergency ambulance with paramedics.

I started Zomato with a spirit of service. Blinkit Ambulance is what that spirit of service looks like today.

In the last 2 years, we have served ~20,000 emergency cases (~42,000 cases in total). We haven't charged a single rupee for any of them. And we want to keep it that way.… https://t.co/lHeo9zo3bN

— Deepinder Goyal (@deepigoyal) November 5, 2026

“We hope that this charge will dramatically drop the usage of our Ambulances for non-emergency cases. 10-minute ambulances have saved and can save thousands of lives, and we need to keep them available for emergencies that need them the most,” Goyal said.

He also highlighted the challenge faced in providing free ambulance services is the availability of paramedics. However, he further added that they are planning to introduce Blinkit Ambulance to all major cities in the country in the next 2-4 years.

item.title: Zoho launches restaurant POS platform, offers free plan for small businesses
item.description: Zoho has launched its restaurant POS platform in India, offering free access to outlets with annual billing of up to Rs 12 lakh, with Kolkata-based Asha Sweets becoming its first customer.
item.content:encoded:
Zoho has launched a point-of-sale (POS) platform for restaurants in India, with Kolkata-based sweet shop Asha Sweets becoming its first customer. The product is being offered free of charge to restaurants with annual billing of up to Rs 12 lakh, as part of Zoho’s push to bring smaller food businesses onto digital platforms.

In a post on X, Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu said Asha Sweets began using Zoho POS for Restaurants during the festive rush. Zoho’s team visited the outlet to observe how the platform was being used during one of its busiest periods.

"The first customer for any new product is special. When that customer is a sweet shop, it is even more special," Vembu said, announcing the launch at Zoholics India.

Zoho POS for Restaurants is a cloud-based platform that brings billing, order management, menu management, kitchen operations and inventory tracking under one system. It is designed for quick-service restaurants, cafes, bakeries, cloud kitchens, casual dining establishments and businesses operating multiple outlets.

The platform consolidates orders from dine-in, takeaway and food delivery channels such as Swiggy and Zomato through a single interface. It also supports QR code-based digital menus, table management and kitchen order tickets (KOTs), which help restaurants track orders and their preparation.

The software supports offline billing, allowing restaurants to continue processing transactions during internet disruptions, with data synchronised once connectivity is restored. It is compatible with Windows and Android devices and integrates with Zoho Books for accounting. Payment integrations include Zoho Payments, Paytm, Pine Labs, and PhonePe.

The product is available under four subscription plans—Free, Essentials, Signature and Premium. While the free plan includes basic billing and inventory management features, capabilities such as food aggregator integrations, table management, self-ordering kiosks and customer loyalty programmes are offered through paid plans.

The launch is part of Zoho's broader expansion into vertical software-as-a-service (SaaS), through which the company is developing industry-specific applications alongside its existing business software. Zoho has identified seven sectors for this expansion, including retail, automotive, banking and financial services, education, real estate and restaurants.

item.title: altM raises $10.3M in Series A funding led by Rainmatter, Mela Ventures
item.description: Bengaluru-based altM will use the funds to expand its manufacturing capacity, strengthen research and development, support customer qualification programmes, and grow its engineering and commercial teams.
item.content:encoded:
Specialty chemicals startup altM has raised $10.3 million in a Series A funding round, with Rainmatter by Zerodha and Mela Ventures joining as new investors. Existing backers Omnivore, Theia Ventures, Aureolis Ventures and Spectrum Impact also participated in the round, along with strategic angel investors.

The Bengaluru-based company said it will use the funds to expand its manufacturing capacity, strengthen research and development, support customer qualification programmes, and grow its engineering and commercial teams. The investment will help altM transition from pilot-scale production to commercial manufacturing.

Founded in 2022 by Apoorv Garg and Yugal Raj Jain, altM uses lignocellulosic biomass, including sugarcane bagasse and rice straw, to produce industrial chemicals. Its processes use the cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin components of biomass to derive multiple products from a single feedstock.

The startup caters to industries such as beauty and personal care, textiles, construction, packaging and consumer goods, with a focus on developing bio-based alternatives to fossil-derived raw materials.

"We are pleased to partner with altM as they move into commercial-scale production. Re-wiring foundational supply chains away from fossil-derived inputs is one of the most critical challenges facing modern manufacturing today," said Abhinav Negi, Lead - Climate & DeepTech, Rainmatter by Zerodha.

"Solving DeepTech problems involves research and understanding interplay of multiple areas. altM is tackling one of the hardest problems in industrial chemistry which is creating new age materials that can match the performance of fossil-derived inputs while fundamentally changing where their carbon comes from," said Krishnakumar N, Managing Partner, Mela Ventures.

Since raising a $3.5 million seed round in 2023, altM has built an integrated research and pilot manufacturing facility in Bengaluru, bringing laboratory research, demonstration manufacturing and pilot production under one roof. The company said it has expanded its laboratory footprint nearly fivefold in less than two years, commissioned a demonstration manufacturing facility, and taken six molecules to demonstration scale. Of these, three have been selected for pilot plant production.

The products being prepared for commercialisation include a lignin-derived SPF booster for suncare, a cellulose-based rheology modifier, and bio-derived ferulic acid for cosmetics and personal care formulations.

"Industrial manufacturing has relied on fossil carbon for more than a century. We are building a new source of industrial carbon from agricultural residue," said Apoorv Garg, Co-founder and CEO of altM. "Our focus is on developing materials and manufacturing processes that allow customers to adopt these materials at the performance, cost, quality, and scale required for industrial applications."

"We've believed in altM from early on, and what makes us double down on our confidence is the team's ability to turn ambitious science into something real and commercially scalable. Going from the lab to reliable manufacturing and, ultimately, customers is a difficult journey. altM has shown a rare ability to make that transition," said Abhilash Sethi, Partner at Omnivore.

item.title: CERT-In warns of security vulnerabilities in Tata Motors' connected vehicle apps
item.description: The vulnerabilities affect specific versions of the apps used by internal combustion engine (ICE) and electric vehicle (EV) owners, raising fresh concerns around cybersecurity risks in connected vehicles.
item.content:encoded:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) on Wednesday flagged multiple high-severity vulnerabilities in specific versions of Tata Motors' iRA 2.0 and iRA.ev connected vehicle applications, warning that they could expose sensitive user credentials, enable user impersonation and allow unauthorised access to vehicle-related information and services.

The vulnerabilities affect iRA 2.0 versions 26.7.3 and below, and iRA.ev versions 26.7.2 and below. The applications cater to Tata Motors' internal combustion engine (ICE) and electric vehicle (EV) customers, respectively, and provide access to connected services such as remote vehicle commands, vehicle status, health monitoring and trip information.

CERT-In identified four vulnerabilities involving hardcoded credentials, inadequate URL validation, exposure of authentication tokens in application logs and improper implementation of SSL certificate pinning.

According to the advisory, these flaws could allow attackers to extract credentials and access backend services, obtain authentication tokens to impersonate users, or intercept and modify communications between the applications and their backend systems.

The vulnerabilities flagged by CERT-In come amid growing cybersecurity concerns around connected vehicles globally. In recent years, security researchers have identified flaws in connected-car platforms operated by automakers such as Kia and Subaru that could potentially expose customer information and enable unauthorised access to vehicle functions.

In another instance, researchers discovered vulnerabilities in Bluetooth software used in vehicles manufactured by Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen, and Skoda, which could potentially allow remote code execution through infotainment systems. These incidents highlight the growing security risks as automakers increasingly rely on mobile applications, cloud infrastructure and connected services to offer digital features to vehicle owners.

item.title: CERT-In warns NBFCs and fintech firms of AI-driven attacks
item.description: An advisory from the government body said the AI-assisted financial threat is still active and warns BFSI entities to treat it as an “immediate and continuing threat”.
item.content:encoded:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has issued an advisory warning that hackers are attacking non-banking financial corporations with the help of artificial intelligence. 

Terming the threat campaign "CRAFTY FALCON", the government body describes it as an “AI-assisted financial threat actor that surveys its targets with machine intelligence, operates at machine speed and strikes by invoking the victim's own payment and disbursement APIs.”

CERT-In is the national nodal agency for responding to computer security incidents.

“Continued analysis of incidents reported by affected entities including non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), digital lending platforms, fintech entities, payment aggregators, payment service providers and cryptocurrency exchanges / virtual digital asset service providers has revealed a significant escalation of this campaign.”

The advisory further said the threat is still active and has warned BFSI (banking, financial services, and insurance) entities to treat it as an “immediate and continuing threat”.

Outlining some of the reported attacks, the advisory said merchant settlement APIs of payment aggregators were exploited or abused to move funds. Cryptocurrency exchanges and virtual digital asset service providers were also targeted, with wallet keys stolen and funds siphoned from cryptocurrency wallets. 

The advisory mentioned that the same companies have faced repeated attacks. 

The body also revealed that its analysis has shown the use of multiple publicly available AI-driven offensive security tools. These include the ARTEX family of LLM-based, the PentAGI autonomous multi-agent AI penetration testing system, the Cairn attack search engine, and the CyberStrikeAI framework. 

Last month, CERT-In had flagged incidents involving AI agents exceeding their authorised tasks and accessing live systems of Indian organisations, alongside financially motivated attacks using open-source agentic AI tools.

Globally too, such attacks have been on the rise. Google’s Threat Intelligence Group reported observing AI offensive security tools being used in real-world intrusions, including attacks on organisations across the United States and Europe.

Edited by Swetha Kannan

item.title: Nykaa's PAT soars 206% in Q2FY27 as beauty, quick commerce arm deliver strong performance
item.description: Nykaa also announced the acquisition of an 82% majority stake in Simply Nam, a cosmetics brand founded in 2020 by celebrity makeup artist Namrata Soni alongside Bozzil, a venture studio led by Hanna Strömgren Khan. The acquisition is expected to help Nykaa widen its premium makeup portfolio.
item.content:encoded:
Omnichannel beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa has reported a profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 101 crore, up 206% in Q2 of FY27 compared with Rs 33 crore a year ago.

Nykaa, which is operated by FSN E-Commerce Ventures, reported Rs. 3,006 crore in revenue from operations, an increase of 28% YoY. 

Its beauty vertical continued to drive the bulk of its business, with a gross merchandise value (GMV) at Rs. 4,454 crore. Meanwhile, its fashion revenue increased 42.9% YoY to Rs 287.2 crore. 

House of Nykaa clocked an annualised GMV run rate of Rs. 4,000 crore, and Rs. 2,300 crore annualised NSV for Q2 FY2027, which is a 36% YoY NSV growth. On the other hand, Superstore by Nykaa has clocked a gross merchandise value (GMV) of Rs 328 crore, and its registered retailer base grew 27% YoY to over 550,000. Net Sales Value or NSV is the actual realised value of goods after the platform accounts for discounts, cancellations, returned items and taxes.

“Our performance this quarter reflects the strength of the Nykaa ecosystem, with each of our businesses contributing to growth and productivity gains. We continued to improve operational efficiency, particularly across marketing and overheads. Beauty and Fashion are seeing accelerated growth, while House of Nykaa and Wellness offer significant runway for long-term growth. We remain focused on building differentiated businesses that serve our consumers and deliver sustainable growth over the long term," Falguni Nayar, executive chairperson, founder and CEO of Nykaa, said.

Nykaa also announced the acquisition of an 82% majority stake in Simply Nam, a cosmetics brand founded in 2020 by celebrity makeup artist Namrata Soni alongside Bozzil, a venture studio led by Hanna Strömgren Khan. The acquisition is expected to help Nykaa widen its premium makeup portfolio.

Nykaa also highlighted the growth of its quick delivery arm, NYKAA Now, which promises 30-to-60 minute delivery. Launched in 2025, the service is available in 15 cities and the company hopes to expand this number to 25 by end of FY2027. Nykaa noted that the vertical offers over 1,000 marquee brands and twice the beauty and personal care (BPC) catalog depth of conventional quick-commerce platforms. The wider selection is reportedly driving an average order value three times higher than typical quick commerce purchases.

Overall, the company has expanded its beauty retail footprint to 338 stores across 111 cities.

item.title: Lenskart's profit doubles, revenue grows 36% in Q2
item.description: The growth was driven by higher eyewear volumes, premiumisation of products, and stronger demand in India and overseas.
item.content:encoded:
Omnichannel eyewear retailer Lenskart's net profit more than doubled in the second quarter of FY27, while revenue rose 36% year on year. The growth was driven by higher eyewear volumes, premiumisation of products, and stronger demand in India and overseas.

Lenskart reported a net profit of Rs 227 crore in Q2FY27 compared to Rs 102 crore in the year-ago period, a growth of 123%. Revenue was Rs 2,845 crore, a YoY growth of 36%.

India revenue grew 35.3% year on year to Rs 1,668 crore, supported by a 26.5% growth in eyewear volumes and rising demand for premium lenses. Same-store sales growth reached 20.8%, compared with 14.8% a year ago. The growth was across metros and Tier I and II+ markets. International revenue grew by 29.5%.

Lenskart added 143 stores in India, including 94 in Tier II+ markets. It also entered 61 new cities. Its India network now spans 2,868 stores across 665 cities. The company conducted 80 lakh eye tests globally, up 40.4% year on year.

Lenskart said it maintained its consolidated product margin at 70%, compared with 69.2% a year ago, despite continued rupee depreciation. In-house frame manufacturing grew 71.7% YoY, while lens manufacturing increased 52.2%, helping offset currency pressures and strengthen control over product quality and costs.

The company has a manufacturing facility in Bhiwadi and is setting up another one in Hyderabad.

Lenskart said it continues to offer technology-enabled eye care, with remote optometry now available in 934 stores across India, compared with 303 a year ago. It also said that AI is increasingly being deployed across customer service, employee training, inventory planning, and manufacturing to improve efficiency and customer experience.

During the second quarter, the company expanded the availability of B by Lenskart, its AI smart glasses, to more than 500 stores across India and online as well.

item.title: PhysicsWallah, Lenskart, Nykaa post stellar profits
item.description: PhysicsWallah posted a record quarterly top-line and doubled its net profit in Q2FY27. Lenskart’s net profit too rose over two-fold year on year. Nykaa’s profit grew three times, and revenue rose 28% YoY.
item.content:encoded:
Dear Reader, 

The earnings season is in full swing. 

PhysicsWallah, Lenskart and Nykaa were among the major Indian companies that reported their Q2FY27 results yesterday. 

Expanding scale and cost efficiencies helped PhysicsWallah post a record quarterly top-line and double its net profit. Lenskart’s net profit too rose over two-fold year on year. 

Nykaa’s profit grew three times to Rs 101 crore and revenue rose 28% YoY to Rs 3,006 crore. The beauty and fashion retailer has also acquired an 82% stake in cosmetics brand Simply Nam. The acquisition is expected to help Nykaa expand its premium makeup portfolio.

Meanwhile, Nasdaq-listed SaaS company Freshworks posted a net profit of $18.3 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with a loss of $4.7 million in the year-ago period. Revenue rose 14% year on year to $245.4 million. 

In an important step towards Atmanirbhar Bharat, the Cabinet has approved a Rs 2,814-crore scheme to promote processing of critical minerals such as lithium and nickel and reduce import dependence. 

In other news, Razorpay has secured Sebi’s approval for its proposed IPO of Rs 5,000-6,000 crore, according to sources. The fintech firm is targeting a valuation of around $5 billion through the public offering. 

Lastly, the Democrats have taken control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the US midterm elections, with Indian Americans also making a mark.

Retail

Lenskart’s profit doubles, revenue grows 36% in Q2

Omnichannel eyewear retailer Lenskart’s net profit more than doubled in the second quarter of FY27, while revenue rose 36% year on year. The growth was driven by higher eyewear volumes, premiumisation of products, and stronger demand in India and overseas.

The company reported a net profit of Rs 227 crore in Q2FY27 compared to Rs 102 crore in the year-ago period, a growth of 123%. Revenue was Rs 2,845 crore, a YoY growth of 36%.

Key takeaways: 

  • India revenue grew 35.3% year on year to Rs 1,668 crore, supported by a 26.5% growth in eyewear volumes and rising demand for premium lenses. Same-store sales growth reached 20.8%, compared with 14.8% a year ago. International revenue grew by 29.5%.
  • The company added 143 stores in India, including 94 in Tier II+ markets. It also entered 61 new cities. Its India network now spans 2,868 stores across 665 cities. 
  • Lenskart maintained its consolidated product margin at 70%, compared with 69.2% a year ago, despite continued rupee depreciation. In-house frame manufacturing grew 71.7% YoY, while lens manufacturing increased 52.2%, helping offset currency pressures and strengthen control over product quality and costs.

Edtech

PhysicsWallah posts Rs 1,242 Cr top-line; net profit doubles

The second quarter of the 2027 financial year marked a pivotal turn for PhysicsWallah, as expanding scale and cost efficiencies together yielded a record quarterly top-line and a two-fold growth in net profit. The edtech firm achieved its highest-ever quarterly revenue, driven by expanding student enrolments and enhanced course realisations. 

Key takeaways:  

  • Consolidated revenue from operations reached Rs 1,242.26 crore, up 18.2% YoY. Total income, which includes other non-operating receipts, grew 21.5% YoY to Rs 1,334.64 crore. 
  • Consolidated profit after tax doubled to Rs 142.29 crore in the second quarter, rising 104.1% YoY from Rs 69.72 crore. The net profit in Q2FY27 comes after a loss of Rs 87.04 crore in Q1FY27.
  • “We delivered record revenue and a sharp improvement in profitability, while our learner base kept widening across K-12, vernacular and new categories. Our focus remains on scaling affordable, tech-led education with disciplined capital allocation,” said Founder and Chief Executive Officer Alakh Pandey.

News & updates

  • Startup momentum: Indian startups with a valuation of over $500 million rose to 51 in 2026, from 47 in 2025, despite a lower number of AI companies. Their combined value is about Rs 3.3 lakh crore, with an average valuation of Rs 6,400 crore, according to the 2026 ASK Private Wealth Hurun India Gazelle Index report.  
  • Canva restructuring: Graphic design platform Canva is undertaking a major workforce restructuring affecting 1,271 employees, or 22% of its workforce, as it adapts to rapid technological change. In a note to employees, CEO Melanie Perkins described this as the hardest moment in Canva’s 13-year history. 
  • Accounts hack: Nearly 30 Indian investors who trade US shares through Stockal Securities have reported unauthorised access to their accounts, alleging that their blue-chip holdings, worth millions of dollars in total, were sold off without their consent and replaced with shares in a little-known company that subsequently lost almost 60% of its value.
